title: Reverse engineering — the documented truth of what already exists
html:
Reverse engineering — the documented truth of what already exists

Not every project starts from zero. Systems in production, legacy code, an ingestion pipeline that already works — the GOLMET reverse-engineers what exists and turns it into documented truth, so the new workflow is born from what is (never from the model's memory, never from guesses).

What the reverse layer delivers

The REVERSE_REPORT — the documented analysis of the frozen source: models, API contracts, business rules. Every claim carries its evidence ([file:line @hash]) — the agent cites the source instead of trusting itself.

reverse/CANDIDATES.md — the candidate knowledge queue (CAND-NNN): what was discovered from the legacy enters the new workflow as a candidate, not as an assumption. This is the bridge between what exists and what will be built (see artefatos.md).

The human layer of the legacy (gm-legacy-guide) — reverse/guide/: OVERVIEW, IMPACT_MAP, GUIDES/, FORMS/ — the guided reading that lets a human validate what the AI documented, domain by domain, with confirmation forms.

The UI golden master (gm-ui-capture) — the visual capture of the legacy flows via the MCP Playwright browser: the old system also has an appearance, and appearance is documented truth too.

The principle: evidence, not memory

The reverse layer's discipline is the same as the knowledge shelf's, taken further: every statement about the legacy carries the file, the line and the commit hash. When the AI is unsure, it declares what it does not know instead of guessing. The human reads, confirms or rejects, and the confirmed truth becomes the foundation the new system builds on.

Where it enters the journey

Brownfield projects start here: analyze the frozen source first, seed the candidate queue, hand the human the guided reading — and only then plan the new workflow on top of documented truth. See 02-projeto.md (the candidate queue in brownfield projects) and 05-maturity-and-knowledge.md (what remains when the project ends).
